history.origins: Piquet is one of the oldest card games still played. First mentioned as Le Cent in Rabelais (1535). Well established by 1650 with rules similar to today; early form used a 36-card pack and first to 100. Introduced in Germany during the Thirty Years' War; popular in France until the early 20th century. Spread to England after Mary I's marriage (1554), then under the French name after Charles I's marriage (1625). Cavendish codified authoritative rules in 1882.
timeline: Present: One of the best 2p games.

rules.objective: Score more over 6 deals. Rubicon: loser <100 pays sum+100; loser â‰¥100 pays difference+100.
rules.gameplay: 1. Exchange: Elder 1-5, Younger 1 to remainder. 2. Declarations: Point (longest suit), Sequence (tierce to huitiÃ¨me), Set (trio, quatorze). Elder declares; Younger says good/not good/equal. 3. Play: No trump; follow suit. Point per lead; extra for winning opponent's lead; last trick +1. 10 for most tricks (40 capot). Repique: 30 in declarations before opponent = +60. Pique: 30 before opponent scores = +30 (elder only).
keyRules: Point, Sequence, Set declarations. Best wins category.

strategy.basic: Elder: exchange 5, go for best hand. Younger: keep stops (e.g. Qxx).
strategy.intermediate: Sink declarations when beaten. Track discards.
strategy.advanced: Throw-in play. Last hand: minimise loser's score if <100.
tips: Point compared by total face value.
